page.layout: One printed page, one text column with a running head at the top; a small section-end line ("DE" with "E" at the lower right) below the text. No marginal notes.

main_text.p: Corroborantia sunt, quæ vires à purgatione, multoq; magis vi morbi debilitatas instaurant: Atque insuper relictas in visceribus obstructiones & intemperies curant & amovent.
main_text.head: Quænam sunt foris admovenda?
Quid sunt Unguenta?
main_text.p: Sunt medicamenta ex oleo, cera, & speciebus certis, tumoribus præter naturam, & ulceribus potissimum destinata.
main_text.head: Quid sunt Cerata vel Cerota, Zugpflaster?
main_text.p: Sunt medicamenta ex oleis, cera aut resina & speciebus certis, unguentis crassiora & solidiora.
main_text.head: Quid sunt Emplastra, dicte salben?
main_text.p: Sunt medicamenta ab unguento differentia crassitie speciérum ingredientium. Emplastra, dicte salbe/ imponuntur vulneribus: Cataplasmata, pflaster/ulceribus: Malagmata, weichpflaster/ super integram cutem injiciuntur.
main_text.head: Quotuplicia sunt Emplastra?
main_text.p: Hæc de Therapeutice: sequitur appendix de remediis dispensandis.
main_text.head: Quibus modis remediorum quantitas dispensatur?
main_text.p: Herbæ dispensantur manipulis: quorum nota est M.
Flores pugillis: quorum nota est P.
Radices, Liquores & Pulveres dispensantur scrupulis, drachmis, unciis, libris: quorum notæ sunt, ℈. ʒ. ʒ. ℔. Fructus numeris, i ij.iij.iiij.v.
Ana, id est, uniuscujusq; speciei, eines jeden.
Lecturus præcepta prolixiora, legat Fernelium, Fuchsium, Hippocratem, Galenum & alios.
Hactenus est Medicina tradita: sequitur de Musica.

page.notes: Printed "eft", "ceres" and similar long-s forms were normalised to s. The German glosses (Zugpflaster, dicte salben, weichpflaster, eines jeden) are set in black letter in the scan and are marked as such where they stand; the exact black-letter forms in the top line of the Cerata entry and the glosses "pflaster/ulceribus" are read with some uncertainty. The "Quid sunt Cerata" head contains a black-letter gloss ("Zugpflaster") that is partly illegible. Dose symbols in the Radices line (℈, ʒ, ℔) are approximate readings of the printed signs. The paragraph "Ana, id est..." is partly obscured. The word "visceribus" contains a possible Cyrillic-looking letter; it should be read as Latin e. Heavy staining at lower left and at the "injiciuntur" line; the final word of that line is partly covered by a dark blot.
